limitations: Sampled elapsed times are not fixed native durations or service guarantees. Sequential snapshots are not an atomic status/readiness oracle.
One fresh source and one target per restore type; source-age causal effect and exact internal scheduling origin cannot be identified from this sample.

evidence.observation: Actor account was checked before mutation. All three unique owned table names were absent and their ALL backup inventories empty before creation. One empty PAY_PER_REQUEST source, one USER backup and exactly one accepted restore from each of that backup and the live PITR source were created. No items or indexes were written. Backup admission CREATING at 27 was separately observed AVAILABLE at 28; restore admission CREATING was not treated as successful physical completion.

The fresh source first has a DescribeTable CREATING snapshot while continuous-backup APIs return TableNotFoundException. Later descriptions expose ContinuousBackupsStatus DISABLED and valid enable returns ContinuousBackupsUnavailableException, with invalid period 36 returning ValidationException. Source readiness is observed ENABLED at 22, enable accepted at 23, and PITR ENABLED separately described at 26. This is fresh creation, not evidence that restore readiness follows the same elapsed-time schedule.

For BOTH restore kinds, current DescribeTable CREATING snapshots bracket DescribeContinuousBackups and valid disable/enable returning TableNotFoundException immediately after successful restore admission. RecoveryPeriodInDays 36 returns ValidationException instead. The backup APIs initially do not recognize each restored target despite DescribeTable recognizing its new identity; TableNotFoundException must not be conflated with the later visible-but-unavailable state.

Both restored targets subsequently expose ContinuousBackupsStatus DISABLED and PITR DISABLED while current DescribeTable snapshots remain CREATING. Valid no-op disable AND valid enable return ContinuousBackupsUnavailableException; invalid period 36 returns ValidationException. This persists late into physical restore, not merely the short initial backup-API visibility gap.

On-demand restore: 272 is CREATING, 273 backups DISABLED, 274/275 valid disable/enable unavailable, 276 invalid period ValidationException, then 277 is the first ACTIVE snapshot. This transition straddles calls and does NOT prove unavailability while continuously ACTIVE. The next backup sample at 288 is ENABLED, no-op disable succeeds at 289, enable is accepted at 290 and separately described ENABLED at 291, then disable succeeds at 292 and is separately described DISABLED at 293. ACTIVE snapshots 287/295 bracket the successful operations.

PITR restore: the last CREATING bracket 266/271 includes backups DISABLED, valid disable/enable unavailable, and invalid-period ValidationException. First ACTIVE is 278, backups are ENABLED at 279, no-op disable succeeds at 280, enable is accepted at 281 and separately described ENABLED at 282; disable at 283 is separately described DISABLED at 284. Invalid period still fails at 285 and 286 remains ACTIVE. This branch does not observe an ACTIVE/unavailable interval.

The source was already ready and PITR-enabled before either restore. Source CreationDateTime 1789773476.549 is retained as SourceTableDetails.TableCreationDateTime in DescribeBackup, but each restored target receives its own CreationDateTime (1789773547.944 on-demand; 1789773552.856 PITR), not the source creation time or restored historical point. Both targets remain backup-unavailable roughly three minutes after admission, long after the fresh source's sampled readiness. An old ready source therefore does not make the target ready, and elapsed time from source creation is not a sufficient readiness predicate. Completion here is observed near first ACTIVE, but this cannot identify whether hidden initialization starts at admission, runs alongside restore, or begins only near physical completion. It does rule out reusing this fresh-source sample's short admission-age threshold as sufficient for these restores.

RestoreSummary is present with RestoreInProgress true while CREATING and absent in first ACTIVE descriptions. The on-demand restore point is backup creation 1789773491.891 and includes SourceBackupArn; PITR uses 1789773489.0 (the described latest bound at 29) and omits SourceBackupArn. Initial, ready-but-PITR-disabled, no-op-disable, and settled-disabled backup responses have only PointInTimeRecoveryStatus inside the PITR description: EarliestRestorableDateTime, LatestRestorableDateTime, RecoveryPeriodInDays and PointInTimeRecoveryWindowDays are omitted, not null. Accepted and separately described enable responses add both retention fields at 1 and equal earliest/latest bounds: 1789773744.0 for PITR target and 1789773754.0 for on-demand target. These are new target recovery intervals, not inherited source bounds or restore timestamps.

Both settled restore targets support strongly consistent scans returning Count 0/ScannedCount 0 with empty Items. PITR DISABLED is separately verified for every table before deletion. The one owned USER backup is deleted and DescribeBackup returns BackupNotFoundException at 323. ALL inventories before and after each table deletion and final inventories show no retained SYSTEM backups; final inventories 330/332/334 are empty without continuation tokens. Final DescribeTable calls 331/333/335 verify all three tables absent. No owned resources remain and no cleanup blocker occurred.

sampledTiming.units: seconds after the successful restore response finished; rounded to milliseconds from captured request timestamps, not an AWS duration guarantee

interpretationLimits: Unlike continuous_backup_readiness.json fresh-creation controls (notably 54-62 and 94-101 there), this restore capture does not establish an interval bracketed by ACTIVE descriptions with unavailable updates. Absence of a sampled interval is not evidence that such an interval is impossible.

The first on-demand backup sample at 288 after first ACTIVE is delayed by sequential sampling of the PITR target. Its 10.943-second observation gap must not be reported as a post-ACTIVE initialization delay.

Only external admission, table status, restore summary, backup status and update responses are observable. The internal scheduler start time and physical readiness instant are not externally identified.

Source-age guard separates source creation from restore admission in this run; it is not an AWS requirement. No old preexisting or days-old source was used, and the capture cannot quantify causal effects of source age.
No CloudTrail events were queried or used to infer asynchronous ordering. Call sequence records client-observed order; accepted update responses are distinguished from separate settled descriptions.
Dense early sampling and later bounded polling can miss transient states. Neither request frequency nor elapsed time is claimed to cause or determine native readiness.

contextCaptures.use: Fresh-creation ACTIVE-before-backup-readiness and passive initialization controls; not substituted for actual restores.
Existing actual PITR restores establish settled restored PITR DISABLED; this capture adds admission-to-readiness sampling.

sources.observation: Restores to a new table and explicitly requires PITR settings to be manually configured on the restored table; no initialization duration specified.
Creates a new table from an existing backup; accepted TableDescription is distinct from settled physical completion.
